"M30x2, G3/4", G7/8", G1", G1¼", NPT3/4", NPT1", NPT1¼", 3/4" BS746, 1" BS746, 1¼" BS746" - environmental_classes: M1 / E2 - ambient_temperature_range: -25°C / +55°C → {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C - gas_temperature_range: -25°C / +55°C → {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C - base_pressure: "Not applicable" — string value "Not applicable" - base_temperature: "Not applicable" - tsp: "Not applicable" — attribute tsp - orientation: "Connection ports vertical" - flow_direction: "Forward flow only (left to right)" - indicating_device: "Electronic" - ancillary_devices: "4G, GPRS or NB-IoT communication module, NFC" - electrical_power: "Lithium battery" - software_identification: "C4, CRC 6087" - manufacturer_trade_mark: INNOVER Model level: - qmax: G1.6=2.5, G2.5=4, G4=6, unit m³/h - qt: G1.6=0.25, G2.5=0.4, G4=0.6, m³/h - qmin: G1.6=0.016, G2.5=0.025, G4=0.04, m³/h - cyclic_volume: 1.2 for all, dm³ - pmax: varies! For G4 aluminium 110mm it's 1.5 bar, else 0.5 bar. So pmax varies per model AND configuration. Hmm. Actually looking at the table: pmax is 0.5 for all except G4 Steel 110mm conn dist is 1.5. Let me re-read: Row 1: G1.6, Alum, 0.5, 130 Row 2: G1.6, Alum, 0.5, 110 Row 3: G2.5, Alum, 0.5, 130 Row 4: G2.5, Alum, 0.5, 110 Row 5: G4, Alum, 0.5, 130 Row 6: G4, Alum, 1.5, 110 Row 7: G1.6, Steel, 0.5, 130 Row 8: G1.6, Steel, 0.5, 110 Row 9: G2.5, Steel, 0.5, 130 Row 10: G2.5, Steel, 0.5, 110 Row 11: G4, Steel, 0.5, 130 Row 12: G4, Steel, 1.5, 110 So pmax = 1.5 bar for G4 with 110mm connection distance (both Alum and Steel), 0.5 otherwise. Cases material: Alum or Steel — this is a configuration axis (material). This is a 3-dimensional situation: size (model) × material × connection distance. Best to capture in matrix_tables with all 12 rows, and model_level for qmax/qt/qmin/cyclic_volume, and config_level for cases_material, pmax, connection_distance. Config level: - axis: "case_material", attribute: cases_material... Actually the axis concept: values keyed by condition. Let me structure config_level: - {attribute: "cases_material", axis: "case material", values: [{condition: "all models", value: "Aluminium"}, ...]} — hmm, better: values: [{condition: "...", value: "Aluminium"}, {condition: "...", value: "Steel"}] Actually the config axis here is two-dimensional (material × connection distance). The cleanest way is matrix_tables with the full 12-row table plus model_level for the flow rates. For config_level, I could do: - attribute: "maximum_pressure", axis: "model × case material × connection distance", values: - {condition: "G4, Alum, 110 mm", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "bar"} - {condition: "G4, Steel, 110 mm", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "bar"} - {condition: "all others", value: 0.5, unit_symbol: "bar"} Hmm, that's a bit awkward. Maybe better to just include pmax in the matrix table rows and keep model_level for the flow rates. But the rules say config_level for attributes that vary by configuration. pmax varies by configuration (material + conn dist). Let me include: config_level: - attribute: "connection_distance", axis: "model × case material", values: [{condition: "all models and materials", value: {min: 110, max: 130}, unit_symbol: "mm"}] — hmm, connection distance is 130 or 110 for every model/material combo. Both options available. Actually let me structure it more naturally: - {attribute: "pmax", axis: "case_material × connection_distance", values: [ {condition: "G1.6/G2.5/G4, Alum or Steel, 130 mm", value: 0.5, unit_symbol: "bar"}, {condition: "G1.6/G2.5, Alum or Steel, 110 mm", value: 0.5, unit_symbol: "bar"}, {condition: "G4, Alum, 110 mm", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "bar"}, {condition: "G4, Steel, 110 mm", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "bar"} ]} Simpler: - {attribute: "maximum_pressure_pmax", axis: "case_material_and_connection_distance", values: [ {condition: "G4 / 110 mm (Alum and Steel)", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "bar"}, {condition: "all other combinations", value: 0.5, unit_symbol: "bar"} ]} That's concise and accurate. And cases_material config: axis "case_material", values: [{condition: "all models", value: "Aluminium"}, {condition: "all models", value: "Steel"}] — or as alternatives. Maybe: {attribute: "cases_material", axis: "case material option", values: [{condition: "available option", value: "Aluminium"}, {condition: "available option", value: "Steel"}]}. Hmm, slightly awkward but conveys. Actually maybe simpler to keep cases_material as a type-level characteristic listing alternatives: {value: "Aluminium or Steel"}. That's fine for a string. Matrix table: full 12-row table with columns size, designation, qmax, qt, qmin, cyclic_volume, cases_material, pmax, connection_distance. Include column_units. Model ids: G1.6, G2.5, G4. Now the certificate number format: "R137/2012-A-IT2-25.01 rev.01". Number field: "R137/2012-A-IT2-25.01 rev.01". Scheme A appears in "OIML CERTIFICATE ISSUED UNDER SCHEME A". Project number: 25.01 (from TER25.01 and cert number IT2-25.01). I'll include project_number: "25.01". Date issued: 12 May 2025 → "2025-05-12". Revision history revision as string: "0" and "1". Recommendation: id "R137", edition 2012, amendment "2014" — schema says amendment... could be string "Amendment 2014" or "2014". The schema shows `edition (int)`, `amendment` — I'll use "2014" or "Amendment 2014". Let me use "2014". Actually safer: "Amendment 2014". Hmm. The markdown: "Edition (year): 2012, including Amendment 2014". I'll put amendment: "2014". The schema doesn't specify type; string "2014" is fine. accuracy_classes: ["1.5"]. Footnotes: none present. It's in the label drawings, so it applies. I'll include: ex_marking: {value: "Ex ia IIA T3 Gb"}. And IP65: ingress_protection: {value: "IP65"}. Standards: EN1359:2017, OIML R137-1&2:2012, EN16314. These are label content — I might include a characteristic "standards_marked": "EN1359:2017, OIML R137-1&2:2012, EN16314". Hmm, optional. I'll include IP65 and Ex marking since they are meaningful technical characteristics. Keep it modest. Also environment class M1/E2, ambient temp -25/+55 (matches label Ta & Tg -25~+55). Connection threads: string value. Software identification: "C4, CRC 6087". Type-level characteristics with structured values. For string values, the schema requires value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers shape. For strings, unit_symbol: null. Attributes with "Not applicable" — record as string "Not applicable"? Rule 8 says don't fabricate; "Not applicable" is a value present in doc. I'll include base_pressure, base_temperature, tsp as "Not applicable" strings. Or omit? I think including with value "Not applicable" is faithful. Labels: t_sp attribute — canonical label "t_sp" or "tsp". Use "t_sp". Connection threads size: value string: "M30x2, G3/4\", G7/8\", G1\", G1¼\", NPT3/4\", NPT1\", NPT1¼\", 3/4\" BS746, 1\" BS746, 1¼\" BS746" — need proper JSON escaping of quotes. Orientations etc as strings. Ambient temperature range: {min: -25, max: 55}, unit_symbol: "°C". Ancillary devices: "4G, GPRS or NB-IoT communication module, NFC". Now model_family: { "family_name": "Smart diaphragm gas meter", — hmm, is that an explicit family name? The type is "Smart diaphragm gas meter". I'll set family_name: null since no explicit family name; description covers it. Actually "Smart diaphragm gas meter" is the type description. family_name null. "models": [{"model_id": "G1.6"}, {"model_id": "G2.5"}, {"model_id": "G4"}] } model_level entries: - qmax m³/h: G1.6: 2.5, G2.5: 4, G4: 6 - qt m³/h: 0.25, 0.4, 0.6 - qmin m³/h: 0.016, 0.025, 0.04 - cyclic_volume dm³: 1.2 all (constant — could be type level; since constant, put in type_level: cyclic_volume: {value: 1.2, unit_symbol: "dm³"}) pmax varies by config, not purely by model — keep in config_level and matrix table. Matrix table name: "Flow characteristics by size and case material". Columns: ["size", "designation", "qmax", "qt", "qmin", "cyclic_volume", "cases_material", "pmax", "connection_distance"] Column units: [null, null, "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h", "dm³", null, "bar", "mm"] Rows (12): with the G4 110mm pmax 1.5 quirk. Wait — check row 6: `1.5` yes, G4 Alum 110 has 1.5. And row 12: G4 Steel 110 also 1.5. All others 0.5. Hmm wait, is that plausible? Actually gas meters G4 often have higher pmax... whatever, extract as-is. Value could be string "110 or 130"? Better: two entries {condition: "option A", value: 130}, {condition: "option B", value: 110}. Or just leave it in matrix table. I'll include config_level entry with values listing both conditions: {attribute: "connection_distance", axis: "connection port variant", values: [{condition: "variant 1", value: 130, unit_symbol: "mm"}, {condition: "variant 2", value: 110, unit_symbol: "mm"}]} Hmm, "variant 1/2" is a bit fabricated-ish but it's a reasonable encoding. Alternatively skip since matrix table captures it. I'll include it for completeness with conditions "Alum and Steel cases, all sizes" ... actually connection distance options apply to all. I'll do: values: [{condition: "all models and case materials", value: {min: 110, max: 130}, ...}] — no, min/max implies continuous range. The set is discrete. I'll use two condition entries. Let me finalize and also include model_level for pmax? No — pmax depends on more than model. config_level is right. Also accuracy class 1.5 is type level.
